brief:
The Quincy Institute reports that the Israel lobby's decades-long dominance over U.S. congressional votes on Middle East policy is showing signs of erosion. A growing number of lawmakers, particularly from younger and more progressive ranks, have broken with the traditional consensus on Israeli military aid and settlement policies, introducing dissenting resolutions and amendments at increasing rates.

The shift reflects broader demographic and ideological changes within the Democratic Party and the emergence of Palestinian rights activism among younger voters. While pro-Israel advocacy groups retain substantial financial resources and institutional access, their ability to enforce party discipline on voting has weakened compared to previous decades, the analysis indicates.
title: Israel lobby's political influence begins to wane in US Congress
